competitive_landscape: Transfers today split between Cat Cocos ferries, Air Seychelles / IDC Twin Otters and resort tenders. No foiling incumbent; the high-end, transfer-dependent market is an ideal Navier Experience fit.

journeys.with_navier: A near-instant smooth hop between the two honeymoon islands.

journeys.with_navier: Direct foiling link skipping the transfer.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the entire inner-island mesh — Mahé, Praslin, La Digue and the closer private islands — plus all resort and airport transfers.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) reaches the outer atolls (Desroches, Alphonse, Aldabra group) on long Indian Ocean trunks beyond Pioneer range.

precedents.why_it_matters: Seychelles reproduces the Maldives high-spend resort-transfer pattern with shorter, denser inner-island legs.

regulatory_note: Seychelles flag; Seychelles Maritime Safety Authority (SMSA) certification; tourism concessions via Seychelles Tourism Board; private-island resorts control their own jetties.
seasonality: Year-round destination; calmest seas Apr–May and Oct–Nov; southeast trade winds (May–Sep) bring chop the foil rides through.
summary: Seychelles is one of the world's premier high-end island destinations, built almost entirely on inter-island transfers between Mahé, Praslin and La Digue plus a constellation of private-island resorts (North Island, Six Senses Zil Pasyon, Four Seasons Desroches). Today guests move by Cat Cocos ferry, small Twin Otter flights and resort tenders. The core inner-island legs sit comfortably inside Pioneer II range, and the high-spend, low-volume profile is an ideal match for the Navier Experience hospitality model.
tagline: A flagship Indian Ocean luxury island-hopping market — short inter-island hops between Mahé, Praslin and La Digue.
